questions.title: Looping with range(1, 5)
questions.prompt: What will this Python code print? Explain your reasoning.
questions.expected_reasoning: range(1, 5) starts at 1 and stops before 5 (exclusive upper bound), generating 1, 2, 3, 4.

questions.title: Iteration Count of range(5)
questions.prompt: How many times does this loop execute, and what is the last value printed? Explain your answer.
questions.code:
count = 0
for i in range(5):
    count += 1
print(f"Total: {count}, Last: {i}")
questions.expected_reasoning: range(5) generates 5 numbers (0, 1, 2, 3, 4), so the loop runs exactly 5 times and the last value is 4.

questions.title: Conditional Assignment Check
questions.prompt: What happens when this Python code runs? Will it print 'Access Granted'? Explain why or why not.
questions.expected_reasoning: 'status = admin' is an assignment statement, which is invalid syntax inside an if statement. Python requires '==' for equality comparison.

questions.title: Variable Modification in Function
questions.prompt: What will this code print? Explain what happens to the variable val inside and outside update().
questions.code:
val = 20

def update():
    val = 50
    print('Inside:', val)

update()
print('Outside:', val)
questions.expected_reasoning: Assigning val = 50 inside update() creates a local variable that shadows the global one. The outer val remains 20.

questions.title: Recursive Countdown Function
questions.prompt: What does this recursive function return when called as countdown(3)? Explain how execution progresses.
questions.expected_reasoning: There is no base case (stopping condition) to halt recursion, so n decrements into negative numbers until RecursionError is raised.

questions.title: Default List Accumulator
questions.prompt: What will the two print statements output? Explain why they produce those lists.
questions.code:
def append_item(x, items=[]):
    items.append(x)
    return items

print(append_item('apple'))
print(append_item('banana'))
questions.expected_reasoning: The default argument items=[] is evaluated once when the function is defined. Subsequent calls mutate that same shared list instance.

questions.title: While Loop Variable Modification
questions.prompt: What exact sequence of numbers will this code output? Explain your tracing of the loop.
questions.expected_reasoning: In the first iteration x becomes 2 and prints 2. Then x < 3 is still true (2 < 3), so in the second iteration x becomes 3 and prints 3. Then 3 < 3 is false, so it terminates.

questions.title: Integer vs Float Division
questions.prompt: What will both print statements output? Explain the difference between / and //.
questions.expected_reasoning: 7 / 2 performs float division giving 3.5. 7 // 2 performs floor division, rounding down to the nearest integer, giving 3.

questions.title: Accessing List Elements
questions.prompt: What will this code print? What element is at index 1 and index -1?
questions.expected_reasoning: Python lists are 0-indexed, so colors[0] is 'red' and colors[1] is 'green'. Negative index -1 accesses the last element 'yellow'.

questions.title: Compound Boolean Evaluation
questions.prompt: What does this code evaluate to? Explain how Python groups the operators.
questions.code:
result = True or False and False
print(result)
questions.expected_reasoning: In Python, 'and' has higher operator precedence than 'or'. So 'False and False' evaluates first to False, then 'True or False' evaluates to True.

transfer_reassessment_questions.title: Transfer Check: Local Shadowing in Helper
transfer_reassessment_questions.prompt: What does this code print? Explain whether the outer counter changes.
transfer_reassessment_questions.code:
counter = 5

def increment():
    counter = 10
    return counter

increment()
print(counter)
transfer_reassessment_questions.expected_reasoning: The function assigns to a local counter, leaving the outer counter unchanged at 5.

transfer_reassessment_questions.title: Transfer Check: Adding Base Case to Recursive Factorial
transfer_reassessment_questions.prompt: What is missing from this recursive function to prevent an infinite loop? Provide the corrected code.
transfer_reassessment_questions.expected_output: Base case guard (e.g., if n <= 1: return 1)
transfer_reassessment_questions.expected_reasoning: A base case is required to stop recursion when n reaches 1 or 0; otherwise it calls factorial indefinitely.

transfer_reassessment_questions.title: Transfer Check: Default Dictionary Mutable Aliasing
transfer_reassessment_questions.prompt: What does record_entry('key1', 'val1') followed by record_entry('key2', 'val2') return? Explain why.
transfer_reassessment_questions.code:
def record_entry(k, v, store={}):
    store[k] = v
    return store

record_entry('a', 1)
print(record_entry('b', 2))
transfer_reassessment_questions.expected_reasoning: The default dictionary store={} is shared across all function calls, retaining keys from previous invocations.
